divergences.topic: Fee (ujrah) on kafalah — may a guarantor charge?
divergences.why_it_matters: The Kafalah demo's showcase scenario: same contract, divergent living answers.
standard_refs: CBUAE HSA Resolution: fees for Letters of Guarantee/Credit (Kafalah)

positions.position: Not permissible to take remuneration for issuing a letter of guarantee, with or without cover, where the remuneration is consideration for the guarantee itself (expense recovery treated separately).
positions.basis: SS 5 text
positions.detail_long: Who: AAOIFI (the Accounting and Auditing Organization for Islamic Financial Institutions) issues the Shari'ah, accounting and governance standards for the industry. Its Shari'ah Standards are mandatory in Bahrain, its home jurisdiction, and adopted in the UAE and other countries. What: Not permissible to take remuneration for issuing a letter of guarantee, with or without cover, where the remuneration is consideration for the guarantee itself (expense recovery treated separately). Why here: the question is “Fee (ujrah) on kafalah — may a guarantor charge?”. The Kafalah demo's showcase scenario: same contract, divergent living answers. Source: SS 5 text
positions.internal_ref: DV01[0] | original source note: SS 5 text read verbatim from ss1.txt 2026-07-18

positions.position: Permits the fee: the guarantor may charge for the kafalah service, as a fixed amount or a percentage of the guaranteed amount.
positions.basis: BNM Kafalah PD 15.1-15.2
positions.detail_long: Who: Bank Negara Malaysia issues a policy document for each contract, and the rulings of its Shariah Advisory Council are binding in Malaysia. What: Permits the fee: the guarantor may charge for the kafalah service, as a fixed amount or a percentage of the guaranteed amount. Why here: the question is “Fee (ujrah) on kafalah — may a guarantor charge?”. The Kafalah demo's showcase scenario: same contract, divergent living answers. Source: BNM Kafalah PD 15.1-15.2
positions.internal_ref: DV01[1] | original source note: BNM Kafalah PD 15.1-15.2, read verbatim 2026-07-17 (20170417-pd-kafalah_130417-revised.txt)

positions.position: Resolution 136/6/2020 (10 Dec 2020, effective 1 Jul 2021): the issuing bank 'may charge an amount equal to the value of actual expenses'; additional amounts only within the stated parameters, and 'it is impermissible to charge an additional amount above the Actual Expenses in exchange for issuing a Guarantee if the Guarantee resulted into a loan' — such excess must be returned to the client or transferred to charity; fees must not be 'a pretext to collect interest (riba)'.
positions.basis: centralbank.ae official PDF (HSA Resolution 136/6/2020, parameters for LG/LC fees).
positions.detail_long: Who: The Higher Shari'ah Authority of the Central Bank of the UAE issues resolutions that sit on top of the AAOIFI standards, which the UAE adopted in 2018. What: Resolution 136/6/2020 (10 Dec 2020, effective 1 Jul 2021): the issuing bank 'may charge an amount equal to the value of actual expenses'; additional amounts only within the stated parameters, and 'it is impermissible to charge an additional amount above the Actual Expenses in exchange for issuing a Guarantee if the Guarantee resulted into a loan' — such excess must be returned to the client or transferred to charity; fees must not be 'a pretext to collect interest (riba)'. Why here: the question is “Fee (ujrah) on kafalah — may a guarantor charge?”. The Kafalah demo's showcase scenario: same contract, divergent living answers. Source: centralbank.ae official PDF (HSA Resolution 136/6/2020, parameters for LG/LC fees).
